narrative.summary: The Bahamas has no AI-specific law, strategy or guidance yet. Its main AI-relevant rule is the Data Protection Act, 2025, passed in December 2025 but not yet in force, whose definition of profiling expressly includes AI and which regulates solely automated decisions and requires data protection impact assessments. Until it commences, the 2003 data protection act remains in force. A national AI policy white paper and an AI bill creating an AI Authority have been announced but not published.

instruments.current_status: Act No. 74 of 2025, assented to 9 December 2025 and published in the Official Gazette (Supplement Part I, No. 50) on 11 December 2025. Not yet in force: s.1(2) leaves commencement to a Minister's notice in the Gazette (possibly by provision), and the laws.bahamas.gov.bs 'Not in force' list still includes it in October 2026. On commencement it repeals and replaces the Data Protection (Privacy of Personal Information) Act (Ch. 324A). The draft Bill went to public consultation by the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner from 21 August 2025 and was tabled in the House of Assembly on 8 October 2025.
instruments.summary: GDPR-style data protection law that will repeal and replace the 2003 Act, covering public- and private-sector data controllers and processors. It defines 'profiling' to include processing that uses artificial intelligence or other algorithmic techniques, and s.50 gives data subjects a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing or profiling that produce legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions (contract, written law, consent) that require safeguards and stricter conditions for sensitive data. It also provides for data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing (s.51), registration of controllers and processors, breach notification, and Commissioner-issued codes of practice, guidelines and certification standards (s.22).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The Bahamas' only enacted legal provision that expressly covers AI: it regulates AI-based profiling and solely automated decisions, and provides for impact assessments of high-risk processing.

instruments.current_status: In force since 2 April 2007 (S.I. 25/2007); assented to 11 April 2003 (the date shown is the assent date, the only date of enactment the revised text states). The Data Protection Act, 2025 repeals and replaces it once commenced by Gazette notice; that had not happened as of October 2026. Revised edition text (LRO 1/2008) read.
instruments.summary: The Bahamas' current data protection law, based on the 1980 OECD Guidelines, regulating the collection, processing, keeping, use and disclosure of personal data by public and private data controllers. It gives individuals rights of access, rectification or erasure and to prohibit direct-marketing processing, and creates the Data Protection Commissioner with enforcement notices, information powers, codes of practice and controls on transfers abroad. It contains no AI- or automated-decision-specific provisions, but it governs personal data used to train and run AI systems until the 2025 Act commences.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law in force; governs personal data processed by AI systems (no AI-specific provisions).
